sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know reported speech with *dijo que* and tense shifting from B1 Unit 13: after a past verb such as *dijo*, the present moves to the imperfect, the past moves to the pluperfect and the future moves to the conditional. You also know *según* + a source from the same unit. They are the tools for writing about a painful period fairly: you say who said what instead of stating a judgement yourself.

sections.title: From direct words to reported words
rows: «Vivo con miedo.» → Dijo que vivía con miedo.
«Vi a los soldados.» → Dijo que había visto a los soldados.
«Hablaré con el juez.» → Dijo que hablaría con el juez.
Según la comisión, hubo miles de víctimas.

items.spanish: La comisión dijo que unas doscientas mil personas habían muerto o desaparecido.
items.english: The commission said that about two hundred thousand people had died or disappeared.

items.spanish: Menchú contó que su familia había sufrido la persecución del ejército.
items.english: Menchú said that her family had suffered persecution by the army.

items.spanish: Según el informe, la mayoría de las violaciones había sido cometida por agentes del Estado.
items.english: According to the report, most violations had been committed by agents of the state.

items.spanish: El tribunal dijo que el exgeneral era culpable.
items.english: The court said that the former general was guilty.

sections.content: Move the verb back after a past reporting verb, and change the pronouns and time words too: *hoy* becomes *aquel día*, *aquí* becomes *allí*. Say who is speaking: a claim about the conflict is always *según la CEH*, *dijo la comisión* or *contó Menchú*, never a statement in your own voice.
